{{verse|chapter=13|verse=1|align=float}}{{outside L|The Epi{{ls}}tle vpon the Sunday of Quinquage{{ls}}me, called Shroue{{ls}}unday.}}{{dropinitial|I}}{{sc|F}} I {{ls}}peake vvith the tonges of men and of Angels, and haue {{sup|‖}} not charitie: I am become as {{ls}}ounding bra{{ls}}{{ls}}e, or a tinkling cymbal. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=2|align=float}}† And if I {{ls}}hould haue prophecie, and knevv al my{{ls}}teries, and al knovvledge, and if I {{ls}}hould ∷ {{outside L|∷ This proueth that faith is nothing vvorth to {{ls}}aluation vvithout vvorkes, and that there may be true faith vvithout Charitie.}} haue al faith {{ls}}o that I could remoue mountaines, and haue not charitie, I am nothing. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=3|align=float}}† And if I {{ls}}hould di{{ls}}tribute al my goods to be meate for the poore, and if I {{ls}}hould {{sup|‖}} deliuer my body {{ls}}o that I burne, and haue not charitie, it doth profit me nothing.
